summary_en: ETS Group raised its FY2026 September final dividend forecast from 23.00 yen to 26.00 yen per share. Despite special losses of 130.0 million yen for construction rectification and 73.3 million yen for asset impairment, operating profit exceeded prior guidance due to improved profitability in electrical construction operations, supporting the dividend increase toward the company's 30% minimum shareholder return target.
title_en: Notice Regarding Recording of Special Losses and Special Gains and Revision of Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
ETS Group announced a revision to its FY2026 September dividend forecast on November 13, 2026. The final dividend per share will be increased from the previously announced 23.00 yen to 26.00 yen, representing a 3.00 yen increase. This decision was made by the Board of Directors despite the company recording two material special charges against earnings for the fiscal year.

The special losses comprised 130.0 million yen for construction rectification costs related to electrical equipment installation work conducted by subsidiary ETS Line between fiscal 2022 and 2026, and 73.3 million yen in impairment losses on solar power generation facilities held by ETS Line. Partially offsetting these charges, the company recorded a 11.0 million yen reversal of asset retirement obligations as special gains. These items were included in the FY2026 September consolidated results but did not meet materiality thresholds for prompt disclosure.

The dividend increase was supported by stronger-than-expected operating performance. Despite the special charges, consolidated operating profit exceeded the prior forecast, driven by improved work profitability in the electrical construction operations. Accordingly, net income attributable to parent shareholders reached 567 million yen, surpassing the initial forecast of 496 million yen. The company's dividend policy targets a shareholder return ratio of 30% or higher through dividends and shareholder gifts, balancing stable dividend distributions with maintenance of internal reserves necessary to strengthen competitiveness and financial condition.
